row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that Opus answers even the unsure questions confidently in both formats, so its few flags sit on the same questions in both formats and J_F stays near J_N.
row.prior_work: Zhao et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.21701; open 7–8B models, a "probability that your guess is correct" prompt) found verbalized-confidence rejected sets change when only the prompt changes (option shuffling: overlap .61 Mistral-7B, .20 Llama-3.1-8B on MMLU); Kim and Kang 2026 (arXiv:2605.27752; open models up to 72B, no Claude) caution that a threshold set under one prompt may not hold under another. Nothing found on Claude Opus or on a probability-against-frequency pair. Predicts: pass direction, size unknown. In people, single-item confidence and estimated frequency correct differ (Gigerenzer, Hoffrage and Kleinbölting 1991, the confidence-frequency effect; named by the em-dm6f2f2 audit, not opened by this session), a mean-level effect, not set overlap. Adds: the replication invariant 7 owes em-dm6f2f2's Sonnet pass, on the third model, on questions where an overseer's list can exist. The odds (45) sit above the literature row's hit rate because the parent's effect and the dry run below are on this exact statistic; the odds context gives its reason.

row.lesson: "Correcting P12 and P15: a confident model flags too few answers on a random draw for this rule to pass, and dry runs assumed spreads. This bet draws non-claim questions from those Sonnet and Haiku were unsure on, builds every dry-run world from archived numbers, and its odds are 45% (from 18% on the map) because format-effect worlds pass 0.12–0.75."

row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that with the own-guess wording and an open answer the number has one plain referent, so Sonnet's two formats flag nearly the same science questions and D falls below 0.10 in that cell.
row.prior_work: In people, calibration depends on the response format (half-range "my answer is correct" against full-range; Hansson, Juslin and Winman 2003, CogSci Proceedings, as opened by the em-dm6f2f2 audit), and single-item confidence differs from estimated frequency correct (Gigerenzer, Hoffrage and Kleinbölting 1991; named by that audit, not opened here). On models, prompt changes move thresholded confidence sets (Zhao et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.21701, open 7–8B models; Kim and Kang 2026, arXiv:2605.27752, open models). The em-dm6f2f2 re-scout names round-number heaping (Dai and Wang 2026, arXiv:2603.09309, abstract only) as a rival. No paper found separates referent wording from forced answer form for a threshold list (re-scout: `map/reads/remap-2026-11-05-em-dm6f2f2.md`). Predicts: unknown. Adds: the one comparison em-dm6f2f2 bundled, on the questions where its parent found the gap.

row.lesson: "Correcting P8: em-dm6f2f2's rewording changed both the number's referent and the answer form, so its pass could not say which carried the gap.
